implementation_notes: The Servlet API is the pattern's canonical home: the container is the FilterManager, FilterChain is the ordered chain, and a filter's doFilter(request, response, chain) performs pre-processing, calls chain.doFilter(...) or returns without it to block the request, and post-processes afterwards. Filters are declared with @WebFilter or web.xml against URL patterns, so the chain changes without touching the target servlet or controller. This is the right level for transport concerns (encoding, compression, CORS, security headers).
pitfalls: Returning without calling chain.doFilter blocks the resource - intentional for authentication, a bug when accidental.
Filter instances are shared across requests, so per-request state belongs in request attributes or a wrapped request, never in instance fields.
Ordering of @WebFilter filters is container-dependent; when the order is part of the contract, declare the chain explicitly.

variants.name: Spring MVC HandlerInterceptor
variants.implementation_notes: Spring MVC provides a bean-managed chain around the handler: preHandle runs before the handler and returns false to short-circuit, postHandle runs after it before view rendering, and afterCompletion runs after the request completes - the first two in registration order, the completion callback in reverse. Registration happens through WebMvcConfigurer#addInterceptors, and interceptors see the HandlerMethod, so they can make decisions a servlet filter cannot (annotation-driven authorization, per-handler auditing, model enrichment). Choose the servlet filter for transport-level concerns and this one for MVC-semantic ones.
pitfalls: postHandle and afterCompletion are skipped for requests that never reach a handler (static resources, errors before dispatch), so they cannot be the only place a cleanup runs.
Async requests need AsyncHandlerInterceptor; otherwise the completion callbacks run on a container thread that no longer owns the request state.
Interceptor order follows registration, and reverse order for the completion callbacks - the mirror image of a servlet chain, which is a common source of confusion.
